title: Writing Studio
permanentRoutine: Notice → Draft → Test with Audience → Revise → Edit → Publish → Reflect

assessmentModel.weekly: open-book craft checks plus authentic writing artifacts
assessmentModel.correction: below 80% on objective/scored craft components requires targeted correction; writing artifacts require substantive revision against the rubric
assessmentModel.protectedBoundary: browser-local drafts and self-checks do not create transcript credit or evaluator-reviewed publication credit

privacySafety.critiqueRule: Critique the work, craft choices, evidence, clarity and revision—not identity, inherent talent, or private life.

crossCurricularReuse.rule: Existing English and Social Studies resources may support instruction, but Writing Studio owns its own elective sequence, artifacts, assessment, and records.

weeks.title: Voice, Audience & Purpose
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do writers make deliberate choices for a specific audience and purpose?

days.task: Study mentor examples connected to Voice, Audience & Purpose. Mark specific craft choices and infer the writer's audience, purpose, and constraints.
days.evidence: mentor-text annotation for Voice, Audience & Purpose

days.task: Study vocabulary and a worked writing model for Voice, Audience & Purpose. Explain which choices improve clarity, credibility, voice, structure, or effect.
days.evidence: annotated craft model and short imitation exercise

days.task: Create at least two approaches to Voice, Audience & Purpose. Test a change in structure, voice, evidence, detail, or form.
Develop the week's main artifact for Voice, Audience & Purpose. Use a rubric, feedback, or self-review to make substantive revision rather than proofreading only.
Edit for correctness and accessibility, prepare a clean version for the intended audience, and write a short reflection explaining one meaningful revision.

weeks.vocabularyTarget: 5–9 writing/craft terms taught through mentor texts, drafting, revision, and retrieval
